name: Parties and Movements That Built Modern Nations
description: Jacobins, Chartists, Congress, Labour, the Kuomintang, the ANC and Solidarity: the organisations that seized, shared or reshaped power.

checkpoints.name: Clubs and charters
checkpoints.note: The Jacobin Club began as a debating society in revolutionary Paris and, under Maximilien Robespierre, became a force that governed France in the Terror. In Britain the Chartists gathered millions of signatures for votes for working men.

checkpoints.name: New parties
checkpoints.note: The Republican Party formed in the United States in 1854 to oppose the spread of slavery, and Abraham Lincoln won the presidency for it in 1860. In India the Indian National Congress first met in 1885 as a forum for educated Indians' demands.

checkpoints.name: Labour and votes
checkpoints.note: Britain's Labour Party began in 1900 to bring working people's voices into parliament. Women's Social and Political Union, founded in 1903 by Emmeline Pankhurst and her daughters, used disruptive protest to demand the vote for women.

checkpoints.name: Founding years
checkpoints.note: In 1912 Sun Yat-sen's Kuomintang formed in the new Chinese republic, and the African National Congress began in South Africa. In Russia, Lenin's Bolsheviks, the roots of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, took power in 1917.

checkpoints.name: Parties in power and in struggle
checkpoints.note: The Nazi Party became Germany's ruling party in 1933 and led it into World War II. The Chinese Communist Party, under Mao Zedong, won the civil war in 1949 against the Kuomintang. In India the Congress of Gandhi and Nehru led the way to independence in 1947.

checkpoints.name: Movements and transitions
checkpoints.note: The Black Panther Party formed in 1966 in the United States. In Poland the trade union Solidarity, led by Lech Walesa, challenged communist rule from 1980. In 1994 Nelson Mandela led the African National Congress to victory in South Africa's first democratic election.
